same_terminal.method: Stay airside. Follow signs to your departure gate. Allow extra time if you need a passport check on arrival.
same_terminal.notes: Same-terminal connections are the simplest. 45 min may be possible for some short-haul-to-short-haul transfers, but 60 min is the safe minimum.

T2-T3.method: Walking link between Terminal 2 and Terminal 3 (about 10 minutes via the underground walkway).
T2-T3.notes: T2 and T3 are physically very close. No transit train needed.

T2-T4.method: Take the free Heathrow Express transfer train (or Elizabeth line) between terminals. Allow 15-20 minutes for the transit.
T2-T4.notes: Furthest pairing. Build in plenty of buffer.

T2-T5.method: Take the free Heathrow Express transfer train (or Elizabeth line) between Central terminals and T5. Transit is about 5-10 minutes.
T2-T5.notes: Common BA connection if your inbound was a Star Alliance flight to T2.

T3-T4.method: Take the free Heathrow Express transfer train (or Elizabeth line) between Central and T4. Transit is about 10-15 minutes.

T3-T5.method: Take the free Heathrow Express transfer train (or Elizabeth line) between Central terminals and T5. Transit is about 5-10 minutes.
T3-T5.notes: BA codeshares often connect this way.

T4-T5.method: Take the free Heathrow Express transfer train (or Elizabeth line) between T4 and T5. Transit is about 5-10 minutes.
T4-T5.notes: Allow time — you'll need to clear security again at T5.

general_tips: Free transfer trains (Heathrow Express or Elizabeth line) connect all terminals airside-to-airside if you're transit-only.
If you cleared immigration on arrival you'll need to re-enter the airside zone, which means another security screening.
Heathrow's official Minimum Connection Time is the bare minimum. For peace of mind, add 30 minutes.
If your bag is checked through, you generally don't need to collect it between flights — confirm with the airline.
